subject: Temporary quota smoothing & proposed retro credit for June overrun
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightbyte.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightbyte.com
Date: 2027-06-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in June usage — need short-term protection and billing clarity

Hi Jordan,

We had an unexpected load on our customer support AI model over the weekend and burned through our quota for the month. Platform signals indicate a sustained 2x above forecast for a 48-hour window (details attached). We want to avoid repeated overrun charges while we stabilize traffic patterns.

Can Redwood provide a temporary threshold extension or a one-off smoothing credit for the June surge? Procurement will need a clear path on invoicing and a PO amendment if necessary.

Attached: usage_report_q2.csv (summary)

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightByte Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightbyte.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in June usage — need short-term protection and billing clarity

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and for the report. I’m sorry you had to deal with that spike. We can do a short-term plan to reduce immediate overage impact while you stabilize. Proposed approach (quick summary):

- Temporary threshold extension: grant a +30% quota headroom for a 72-hour window (retroactive to the incident start) to absorb legitimate burst traffic
- Pro-rated smoothing credit: apply a one-time credit equal to 50% of the calculated overrun invoice for the burst window
- Billing path: Redwood will issue an interim credit memo and we can amend the June invoice; if you prefer a PO amendment we’ll provide the contract addendum language

Two asks from our side to make this operational: the exact timestamps for the surge window (so we can tie it to logs) and a signed confirmation that the burst was due to production traffic and not a load-test or other non-prod activity.

I’ve looped in Karthik for pricing approval and Ben for the billing/ops steps. If that plan looks reasonable I’ll follow up with a short amendment and a DocuSign link.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-19T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing ok for one-off smoothing credit?

Jordan —

Quick internal: 50% credit on the burst overrun is acceptable for this cohort given the enterprise relationship and signal that this was an operational incident. Approve the +30% for 72 hours.

Ben — coordinate the credit memo and ensure accounting will accept a PO amendment for the residual amount. Keep the credit separate from standard discounts — mark as "incident smoothing".

Karthik
VP, Strategic Accounts
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightbyte.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightbyte.com
Date: 2027-06-22T10:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in June usage — need short-term protection and billing clarity

Jordan —

Thanks, that plan is a good start. Confirming the surge window: 2027-06-12T02:00:00Z to 2027-06-14T06:00:00Z (UTC). The traffic was production (we had a routing config change). Procurement asked if the 50% credit could be increased to 65% if Redwood can also provide a temporary rate-limit bump so we don’t hit the same ceilings while we deploy mitigations. They will also need a one-paragraph statement from Redwood that the credit is a one-time operational concession.

I’ve attached the PO template to make the amendment easy.

—Elena

Attachment: BrightByte_PO_Template.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightbyte.com>, procurement@brightbyte.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-24T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in June usage — need short-term protection and billing clarity

Elena / Procurement team —

Appreciate the clarifying details. Final proposal we can commit to today:

1) Temporary rate-limit/threshold bump: +45% quota headroom for the specified window (2027-06-12T02:00:00Z to 2027-06-14T06:00:00Z) to be applied retroactively so those tokens are reclassified as within the temporary allowance.
2) One-time smoothing credit: 60% of the overrun charges for that window, applied as a credit memo against the June invoice. We can increase to 65% only if procurement confirms a 12-month renewal commitment (to be discussed separately).
3) Documentation: I’ve attached a one-paragraph statement below you can include with your PO amendment. We will also send a DocuSign contract addendum for signature.

Redwood statement for your PO: "Redwood Inference will apply a one-time operational smoothing credit and a temporary quota headroom adjustment to address the documented production surge experienced by BrightByte Health during the period 2027-06-12T02:00:00Z — 2027-06-14T06:00:00Z. This concession is a single-instance operational accommodation and does not change the parties' existing pricing or quota terms."

Next steps from here: Elena — confirm you accept the 60% credit and we’ll kick off DocuSign + credit memo. Procurement — Ben will email the credit memo and instructions for the PO amendment.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: BrightByte_PO_Template.pdf
DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=example-id-4729
